records.label: E410K pedigrees

phenotypes.text: later-onset lower extremity weakness and sensory loss (oldest patient)

records.segregation: arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germline mosaicism; absent in parents
quotes: The remaining mutations, 1138C>T (R380C), 785G>A (R262H), and 1228G>A (E410K), were found in one, two, and six pedigrees, respectively, and each arose de novo as sporadic disease or from presumed germ-line mosaicism
whereas all participants with R262H, E410K, and D417H had severe CFEOM3 and congenital facial weakness
Individuals with A302T, E410K, R262H, and R380C had more severe CC dysgenesis and mild to moderate intellectual, social, and behavioral impairments.

records.label: R262C pedigrees
quotes: We identified three heterozygous TUBB3 missense changes in 15 unrelated pedigrees: 784C>T (R262C) in 11 pedigrees, 904G>A (A302T) in three pedigrees, and 185G>A (R62Q) in one pedigree
R262C can cause bilateral ptosis and severe CFEOM3 with the resting position of both eyes infraducted and abducted (A), moderate CFEOM3 that can be unilateral (B), and mild CFEOM3 (not shown).
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: A302T pedigrees

phenotypes.text: mild to moderate intellectual and behavioral impairment

quotes: A302T (C) and R380C (D) cause moderate to severe CFEOM3.
Subjects with A302T, E410K, and R262H have diffuse CC hypoplasia (D–F).
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: R62Q pedigree
quotes: Brain imaging was reviewed from individuals with each TUBB3 mutation except D417H, and appeared normal only in the R62Q subject.

records.label: D417N pedigrees

phenotypes.text: axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with onset in second to third decade
hypoplasia of posterior body of corpus callosum
pes cavus with intrinsic foot muscle atrophy

records.segregation: co-segregated in a dominant fashion; some carriers had polyneuropathy without CFEOM3
quotes: 1249G>C (D417H) and 1249G>A (D417N) alter the same residue and co-segregate in a dominant fashion in one and four pedigrees, respectively.

Most subjects harboring D417N and the oldest patient harboring E410K developed lower extremity weakness and sensory loss in the second to third decade, all in the absence of congenital contractures (Figure 1F).
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: D417H pedigree

phenotypes.text: lower extremity weakness and sensory loss in first decade

quotes: All subjects harboring D417H or R262H were born with congenital wrist and finger contractures, suggesting maldevelopment of spinal motor neurons (Figure 1I), and developed lower extremity weakness and sensory loss in the first decade of life.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: R262H pedigrees

phenotypes.text: congenital ulnar deviation and finger contractures

records.segregation: de novo or presumed germline mosaicism
quotes: E410K (G) and R262H (H) result in severe CFEOM3 and facial weakness, and R262H also results in congenital ulnar deviation of the hand with joint contractures of the thumbs and fingers (I).
R262H (M) and R380C (N) patient scans show AC agenesis and dysmorphic basal ganglia.

records.label: R380C siblings
records.segregation: presumed germline mosaicism; absent in parents
quotes: (G) Both R380C siblings have CC agenesis, and brainstem (arrow) and mild vermian hypoplasia (asterisk).
CFEOM3 with developmental delay, CC agenesis, and basal ganglia dysmorphisms in the absence of facial weakness may be predictive of the R380C substitution.

records.label: Eight unrelated individuals with TUBB3 E410K

phenotypes.text: congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
hypoplastic to absent olfactory sulci and olfactory bulbs

records.segregation: de novo in eight unrelated individuals
quotes: We report the detailed phenotypes of eight unrelated individuals who harbour this de novo mutation, and thus define the 'TUBB3 E410K syndrome'.

expand the TUBB3 E410K phenotype to include Kallmann syndrome (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia), stereotyped midface hypoplasia, intellectual disabilities and, in some cases, vocal cord paralysis, tracheomalacia and cyclic vomiting.
Neuroimaging reveals a thin corpus callosum and anterior commissure, and hypoplastic to absent olfactory sulci, olfactory bulbs and oculomotor and facial nerves

records.label: Female proband (mother)

phenotypes.text: congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles
hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (normal sexual development at puberty, spontaneous pregnancies)

records.segregation: de novo in proband; transmitted to all three affected sons
quotes: A de novo TUBB3 c.1228G>A mutation arose in a female proband who displayed CFEOM, facial weakness, intellectual and social disabilities, and anosmia.
However, she underwent normal sexual development at puberty and had three spontaneous pregnancies with subsequent autosomal-dominant inheritance of the mutation by her three boys.

records.label: Three affected sons

phenotypes.text: congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscles

records.segregation: inherited from affected mother by all three sons
quotes: had three spontaneous pregnancies with subsequent autosomal-dominant inheritance of the mutation by her three boys.
All sons displayed nonendocrine features of the TUBB3 E410K syndrome similar to their mother but, in addition, had variable features suggestive of additional endocrine abnormalities.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: 31-year-old Japanese woman

phenotypes.text: decreased sense of smell since childhood
abnormal morphology of the corpus callosum

quotes: The patient is a 31-year-old Japanese woman who was diagnosed with atypical Moebius syndrome because of congenital facial weakness and extraocular ophthalmoplegia sparing abduction.
She also had borderline intellectual disability, cyclic vomiting, syncope with cough, and decreased sense of smell since childhood.
we analyzed the TUBB3 gene and identified a heterozygous c.1228G > A (p.E410K) mutation that confirmed the diagnosis of TUBB3 E410K syndrome.

records.label: Seven unrelated individuals with TUBB3 E410K syndrome

phenotypes.text: bilateral absence of dorsal language network long segment
diffuse decreased fractional anisotropy in white matter (pediatric subjects)

quotes: Seven unrelated individuals (four pediatric, three adults) with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome, harboring identical de novo heterozygous TUBB3 c.1228 G>A mutations, underwent neuropsychological testing and neuroimaging.
Despite the absence of cortical malformations, they have intellectual and social disabilities.
All subjects showed aberrant corticospinal tract trajectory and bilateral absence of the dorsal language network long segment.

records.label: 3-year-old boy

phenotypes.text: severe bilateral palpebral ptosis refractory to eye surgery

quotes: We report on a 3-year-old boy in whom clinical exome sequencing allowed to identify a de novo TUBB3 E410K mutation as the molecular cause underlying a complex phenotype characterized by a severe bilateral palpebral ptosis refractory to eye surgery, psychomotor delay, absent speech, hypogonadism, celiac disease, and cyclic vomiting.
Brain MRI revealed thinning of the corpus callosum with no evidence of malformation cortical dysplasia.

records.label: 11-year-old girl
quotes: An 11-year-old girl has been followed up as having atypical Möbius syndrome since infancy, as she was born with bilateral ptosis, paralytic strabismus, and facial weakness. At age 7 years, she was diagnosed with TUBB3 E410K syndrome by whole-exome sequencing.
At age 10 years, her blood examination revealed elevated liver transaminase levels, which persisted for almost 2 years. She underwent liver biopsy, the results of which were suggestive of NASH.

Facial weakness and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism occurred in the patients harboring E410K and R262H variants.

In present study, three patients with TUBB3 E410K and R262H variants (C21, C32 and C52) fitted the diagnostic criteria of Kallmann syndrome

notes.statement: Jia et al. (2022) found that in CFEOM patients with TUBB3 variants, absence of the facial nerves (CN7) and dysplasia of the olfactory bulbs and sulci were correlated with the R262H and E410K variants. Malformations of the corpus callosum, anterior commissure and lateral ventricle were common to the R380C, R262H and E410K variants.
quotes: Absence of facial nerves (CN7) and dysplasia of olfactory bulbs and sulci (OBS) were correlated with R262H and E410K variants (Figs. 6, 7).
Common features of MRI from patients with R380C, R262H and E410K variants were malformations of the corpus callosum, anterior commissure and lateral ventricle.

notes.statement: Jia et al. (2022) noted that patients with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome were easily misdiagnosed as having Mobius syndrome because of facial weakness and limited eye movements. They suggested that MRI, WES and targeted general examinations can contribute to accurate diagnosis.
quotes: Furthermore, the patients with “TUBB3 E410K syndrome” and “TUBB3 R262H syndrome” were easily misdiagnosed as MBS owing to similar clinical manifestations (facial weakness and limitation of eye movements etc.).

notes.statement: Jia et al. (2022) found that 3 patients with the TUBB3 E410K or R262H variant fitted the diagnostic criteria of Kallmann syndrome. They suggested that TUBB3 may be involved in the pathogenesis of Kallmann syndrome.
quotes: In present study, three patients with TUBB3 E410K and R262H variants (C21, C32 and C52) fitted the diagnostic criteria of Kallmann syndrome, confirmed the previous report results and suggested that TUBB3 gene may involve in the pathogenesis of Kallmann syndrome.

notes.statement: Mori et al. (2022) found that TUBB3 expression was absent but tyrosine hydroxylase expression was present in parenchymal nerve fibers of the liver of a girl with TUBB3 E410K syndrome and NASH, whereas an autopsy NASH case and a normal control showed coexpression of TUBB3 and TH. They suggested that TUBB3 mutation may be associated with the pathogenesis and progression of NASH.
quotes: The expression of TUBB3 was absent, but that of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) was present in the parenchymal nerve fibers of the liver. On the other hand, in comparison with an autopsy case of NASH and a normal control, these showed coexpression of TUBB3 and TH in the liver.
This case suggests that the TUBB3 mutation may be associated with the pathogenesis and progression of NASH in humans.

notes.statement: From a review of reported patients with the TUBB3 E410K mutation compared with patients carrying other TUBB3 mutations, Dentici et al. (2020) concluded that E410K results in a clinically recognizable phenotype that is not associated with the distinct cortical dysplasia caused by other mutations in the same gene.
quotes: The present study confirms that TUBB3 E410K results in a clinically recognizable phenotype, unassociated to the distinct cortical dysplasia caused by other mutations in the same gene.

notes.statement: Dentici et al. (2020) stated that the recurrent heterozygous TUBB3 c.1228G-A (E410K) mutation causes a rare disorder characterized by CFEOM3, intellectual disability, and a wide range of neurologic and endocrine abnormalities, and recommended early molecular diagnosis to enable neurologic, ophthalmologic, endocrine, and gastrointestinal follow-up.
quotes: A recurrent heterozygous mutation, c.1228G > A; p.E410K, in TUBB3 gene is responsible of a rare disorder clinically characterized by congenital fibrosis of the extraocular muscle type 3 (CFEOM3), intellectual disability and a wide range of neurological and endocrine abnormalities.

Early molecular characterization of TUBB3 E410K syndrome is critical for targeted genetic counseling and prompt prospective care in term of neurological, ophthalmological, endocrine, and gastrointestinal follow-up.

notes.statement: Grant et al. (2019) compared structural and diffusion MRI of 7 individuals with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome with 22 controls and found decreased corpus callosum volume and decreased network efficiency; only pediatric subjects had diffuse decreases in fractional anisotropy predominantly affecting mid- and long-range tracts, whereas only adults had white matter volume loss associated with decreased cortical surface area. All subjects showed aberrant corticospinal tract trajectory and bilateral absence of the dorsal language network long segment.
quotes: Subjects had decreased corpus callosum volume and decreased network efficiency. While only pediatric subjects had diffuse decreases in FA predominantly affecting mid- and long-range tracts, only adult subjects had white matter volume loss associated with decreased cortical surface area.

notes.statement: Grant et al. (2019) concluded that their findings defined a TUBB3 E410K neuroimaging endophenotype and hypothesized that the age-related changes are due to microscopic intrahemispheric misguided axons that are pruned during maturation.
quotes: These findings define a TUBB3 E410K neuroimaging endophenotype and lead to the hypothesis that the age-related changes are due to microscopic intrahemispheric misguided axons that are pruned during maturation.

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2018) noted that TUBB3 E410K syndrome may be misdiagnosed as atypical Moebius syndrome because the clinical symptoms overlap. They suggested that testing for the c.1228G>A mutation in TUBB3 is useful for distinguishing it from other disorders with congenital external ophthalmoplegia and facial nerve palsy.
quotes: TUBB3 E410K syndrome may be diagnosed as atypical Moebius syndrome because of overlapping clinical symptoms.
Genetic analysis of c.1228G > A in TUBB3 is useful to differentiate TUBB3 E410K syndrome from other disorders presenting congenital external ophthalmoplegia and facial nerve palsy.

notes.statement: Balasubramanian et al. (2015) reported the first familial, autosomal dominant transmission of the TUBB3 E410K syndrome: a de novo c.1228G>A mutation arose in a female proband and was transmitted to her three affected sons. All previously reported TUBB3 E410K patients had been sporadic cases.
quotes: All TUBB3 E410K subjects reported to date are sporadic cases.

This first report of an autosomal-dominant inheritance of the TUBB3 c.1228G>A mutation in a family provides new insights into the spectrum and variability of endocrine phenotypes associated with the TUBB3 E410K syndrome.

notes.statement: Balasubramanian et al. (2015) found that the reproductive phenotype in TUBB3 E410K syndrome varied. The proband had anosmia but went through normal puberty and had 3 spontaneous pregnancies, while her sons had variable features suggestive of additional endocrine abnormalities. The authors noted that this variability complicated genetic counseling.
quotes: However, she underwent normal sexual development at puberty and had three spontaneous pregnancies
These observations emphasize the need for appropriate clinical evaluation and complicate genetic counseling of patients and families with this syndrome.

notes.statement: Chew et al. (2013) found that the TUBB3 c.1228G>A (E410K) mutation was absent in DNA from about 600 individuals who had Kallmann syndrome or isolated or syndromic ocular and/or facial dysmotility disorders but did not have the combined features of the TUBB3 E410K syndrome. They concluded that the genotype-phenotype correlation was specific.
quotes: the c.1228G>A mutation was absent in DNA from ∼600 individuals who had either Kallmann syndrome or isolated or syndromic ocular and/or facial dysmotility disorders, but who did not have the combined features of the TUBB3 E410K syndrome

notes.statement: Chew et al. (2013) noted that the E410K substitution directly alters a kinesin motor protein binding site. They found that the neuroimaging findings supported underlying abnormalities in axon guidance and maintenance.
quotes: c.1228G>A results in a TUBB3 E410K amino acid substitution that directly alters a kinesin motor protein binding site
which support underlying abnormalities in axon guidance and maintenance

notes.statement: Chew et al. (2013) used electrophysiology to confirm that a progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy segregates with the E410K mutation. They concluded that the E410K substitution defines a new genetic cause of Moebius syndrome, Kallmann syndrome and cyclic vomiting.
quotes: We now confirm by electrophysiology that a progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy does indeed segregate with the mutation
Thus, the E410K substitution defines a new genetic aetiology for Moebius syndrome, Kallmann syndrome and cyclic vomiting.

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) found 8 different heterozygous missense mutations in TUBB3, altering 6 amino acid residues, in 29 unrelated families with CFEOM3, either isolated or with additional neurologic features. None of the mutations was present on more than 1,700 control chromosomes. The R262H, R380C, and E410K mutations arose de novo or from presumed germline mosaicism.
quotes: In 29 unrelated families, we identified eight unique heterozygous missense mutations that alter six amino acid residues.
Each of the eight mutations segregated with the TUBB3 phenotype, was absent in parents of sporadic individuals, and was not present on over 1700 control chromosomes.

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) reported that severe CFEOM3 with facial weakness, developmental delay, moderate to severe corpus callosum dysgenesis, and likely a late-onset polyneuropathy predicted the E410K substitution. Finger contractures, basal ganglia dysmorphisms, and early-onset polyneuropathy suggested R262H or D417H. Most adults with isolated CFEOM3 had R262C.
quotes: Association of severe CFEOM3 with facial weakness, developmental delay, moderate to severe CC dysgenesis and likely a late-onset polyneuropathy predicts the E410K substitution, while the addition of finger contractures, basal ganglia dysmorphisms, and early onset polyneuropathy would suggest R262H or D417H substitutions.
Overall, most adults with isolated CFEOM3 have R262C or, less commonly, R62Q or A302T substitutions.

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) found that brain imaging in patients with TUBB3 mutations showed dysgenesis of the corpus callosum, anterior commissure, and internal capsule, together with basal ganglia dysmorphisms. There was no cortical dysplasia or migration defect. Intellectual and behavioral impairments generally correlated with the severity of corpus callosum dysgenesis.
quotes: Common findings were dysgenesis of the corpus callosum (CC), anterior commissure (AC), and internal capsule; generalized loss of white matter; and basal ganglia dysmorphisms that correlated with specific mutations (Figure 2). No images showed cortical dysplasia or evidence of cortical migration defects.

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) generated Tubb3 R262C knock-in mice. Heterozygotes appeared healthy. Homozygotes died within hours of birth and had cortical layering that was normal, but showed defects in guidance of the anterior commissure, corpus callosum, and cranial nerves. Homozygotes also had increased microtubule stability and reduced Kif21a binding to microtubules.
quotes: By contrast, Tubb3R262C/R262C mice failed to breathe normally and died within hours of birth.
Tubb3R262C/R262C mice showed defects in the guidance of commissural axons and cranial nerves.
A significant decrease of Kif21a was detected with microtubules from the brains of Tubb3R262C/R262C mice (Figure 4E).

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) modeled the mutations in yeast beta-tubulin. All of the substitutions altered microtubule dynamic instability. The R262C, R262H, E410K, D417N, and D417H substitutions reduced plus-end accumulation of the kinesins Kip3p and Kip2p. In rabbit reticulocyte lysate, R62Q, R262C, A302T, and R380C markedly reduced heterodimer yield.
quotes: Thus, the R262C, R262H, E410K, D417N, and D417H substitutions result in a significant decrease in Kip3p-3YFP and Kip2p-3YFP accumulation on microtubule plus-ends
Under native conditions, R62Q, R262C, A302T, and R380C showed significant reductions in heterodimer yield, whereas the remaining four mutants generated moderate yields (Figure 4F).
